items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: La Roca Pete the drummer; they were working with Sonny... Pete sits down at the drums, and Don grabs his bass... Sonny turned to me and says, 'I want to play Old Devil Moon'

ctx.x: Oh, well, one afternoon; no, the previous afternoon, I'm down at the Vanguard and Sonny had come up and he we had a bass player, Don Bailey, out of Baltimore, and La Roca Pete the drummer; they were working with Sonny, and Sonny said, "Hey Wilbur, I want you to come by tomorrow afternoon" -- now they had matinees down at the Vanguard at that time, and he said he was recording down there tomorrow and I want you to come by and do a track on my date."

And he said, "But I'll pay you for the whole date". It wasn't that much -- you know, a whole day I think. It was $50 or $75 or something like that. One side. And two sides, LP was a hundred and a quarter, I believe.
